ui.lunarSecret.title: The Deal
ui.lunarSecret.line5: To the one who saved Earth!
ui.cine.intro.1: Earth has always been our home.
ui.cine.intro.2: We took poor care of it. Rivers shrank, forests faded and the sky changed.
ui.cine.intro.3: Cities began to run short of what they needed.
ui.cine.intro.4: So Project EARTH'S ANGEL was born: learning to live without wasting anything. Four crew members were chosen.
ui.cine.intro.5: Their ship, EL ANGEL, set out for the Moon.
ui.cine.intro.6: First mission: build a shelter where nothing runs out. Earth is counting the days.
ui.cine.moonToMars.1: The Moon base now runs on its own.
ui.cine.moonToMars.3: What they learned is already helping at home. Earth gains {bonus} days.
ui.cine.moonToMars.4: With that time, the Angel sets out for Mars.
ui.cine.moonToMars.5: Commander: This is El Ángel. All four of us have reached Mars.
ui.cine.moonToMars.6: Engineering: Look to the right! Another ship is landing.
ui.cine.moonToMars.7: Geology: We're the backup team. I can locate ice and other resources.
ui.cine.moonToMars.8: Communications: We're here to help! I'll keep us in touch with Earth.
ui.cine.moonToMars.9: Commander: Welcome! There are six of us now. Let's build this base together.
ui.cine.marsVictory.1: Commander: Oxygen, water, and food are stable.
ui.cine.marsVictory.earthFailed: We returned to Mars. Earth still needs help.
ui.cine.marsVictory.2: Engineering: The colony can sustain itself now.
ui.cine.marsVictory.3: Commander: Mars is self-sufficient! We did it, team!
ui.cine.marsVictory.4: Botany: Today's harvest is for everyone!
ui.cine.marsVictory.5: Communications: Earth, this is Mars. The colony is self-sufficient.
ui.cine.marsVictory.6: Earth Control: Copy that. We're already putting what you learned to work.
ui.cine.marsVictory.7: Commander: Today we celebrate what we built together.
ui.cine.marsVictory.8: Commander: And we gave Earth another chance.
ui.cine.wormhole.1: Both beacons wake at once. Something opens above the lab.
ui.cine.wormhole.3: The passage leads to Earth's past.
ui.cine.wormhole.4: Here, there is still time. Project Second Chance.
ui.cine.wormhole.banner: Time travel is part of the story, not real science.
ui.cine.earthVictory.1: What kept the base alive now cares for Earth.
ui.cine.earthVictory.4: The future begins by learning to care for our home. We still have time to protect Earth.
ui.manifest.heading: What travels to Mars
ui.manifest.arrivalNote: Half of the Moon supplies travel with you and are added to the Mars stockpile. Cargo power reads zero because the level starts with its own power.
ui.cards.title: Science cards
ui.learn.reviewPrompt: Now that the Moon mission is over, how would you prepare the base for a solar storm?
ui.result.lunarCheers: We did it, team! The base can sustain itself.
ui.cine.boarding.run: All aboard! Earth is counting on us.
ui.cine.boarding.rescue: Are you all right? Take my hand. We leave together.
ui.cine.boarding.launch: Crew aboard. Lifting off for Mars.
ui.walk.marsArrival: Explore Mars on foot. Q opens field actions and B opens the base. Build a self-sufficient colony and keep the link to Earth running. Dust can reduce solar power.
ui.hud.marsGravity: Mars gravity: 3.73 m/s², about 38% of Earth’s.
ui.practice.power.prompt: The solar panels are in shadow. Where can the base get power?
ui.practice.power.why: Solar panels need light to make electricity. A battery stores energy collected in sunlight and can power equipment while the panels are in shadow.
ui.practice.waterLoop.prompt: What can the Space Station use to recover water?
ui.practice.waterLoop.why: The system collects moisture from the air and treats used water. It tests the recovered water before returning it to the supply.
ui.practice.airFromWater.prompt: How can we get breathable oxygen from water?
ui.practice.airFromWater.B: By straining it through a mesh.
ui.practice.airFromWater.why: Electricity can split water into oxygen and hydrogen. This process is called electrolysis, and the International Space Station uses it.
ui.practice.solarStorm.prompt: A solar storm increases radiation. Where is the crew best protected?
ui.practice.solarStorm.B: In the most heavily shielded area.
ui.practice.solarStorm.why: The material around the shelter reduces the crew’s exposure to the particles. In the game, you also need to save enough power to use the shelter.
ui.learn.prompt: A solar storm reaches your Moon base tomorrow. What should you do first?
ui.learn.B: Have the shelter ready and save power to use it.
ui.learn.C: Turn every machine off to save power.
ui.learn.after: In your mission you saw that the shelter protects, and that using it has a cost.
ui.choice.heading: The colony is safe. What next?
ui.choice.stayBody: The colony is safe. A new chapter begins.
ui.choice.portalBody: The beacons open a path to Earth's past. One last mission.
ui.choice.portalWarning: If the Earth mission fails, you return to the Mars ending. You do not lose that victory.
ui.choice.fiction: Time travel is part of the story, not real science.

ui.earth.closing: What kept the base alive also cares for Earth.

ui.shelter.title: The crew is in the shelter
ui.shelter.body: Particles from the solar storm are passing outside. The thick shelter walls stop most of them, so the crew waits inside today.
ui.shelter.note: No building or exploring today. You can still end the day.
ui.presentation.start: Presentation mode: Earth's Angel plays itself. Press X at any time to stop.
ui.presentation.opening: Earth's Angel: design a space mission on Earth, launch it, and run it on the Moon and then on Mars.
ui.presentation.moon1: Day 1 on the Moon: two solar panels first. Without power, nothing else in the base works.
ui.presentation.moon2: Day 2: an ice extractor and a water recycler. Water is for drinking and for making oxygen.
ui.presentation.moon3: Day 3: the oxygen generator turns water into air, and the greenhouse grows food.
ui.presentation.moon4: Day 4: the panels are in shadow. A battery stores energy for the dark hours.
ui.presentation.moon5: Day 5: we build the radiation shelter before the solar storm arrives.
ui.presentation.moon6: Day 6: one more solar panel, so every system has power.
ui.presentation.moon7: Day 7: the base sustains itself. The forecast warns of a solar storm.
ui.presentation.moon8: Day 8: solar storm! The crew waits it out in the shielded shelter.
ui.presentation.moon9: Day 9: the storm has passed and the base is stable.
ui.presentation.moonStorm: A solar storm is coming: the commander decides whether the crew shelters.
ui.presentation.moonWin: The Moon base works on its own. Next stop: Mars.
ui.presentation.toMars: Half of the Moon supplies travel with the crew to Mars.
ui.presentation.marsArrive: Mars: a sol lasts about 24 h 40 min, dust covers the panels and radio messages to Earth take minutes. The small ship beside the base is the support ship.
ui.presentation.mars1: Sol 1: panels, oxygen generator and greenhouse at once. Mars starts with very little margin.
ui.presentation.mars2: Sol 2: ice extractors. There is frozen water on Mars that the colony can use.
ui.presentation.mars4: Sol 4: dust covers the panels, so the crew cleans them to get the power back.
ui.presentation.mars9: Sol 9: two shelters, so the whole crew of six fits during a solar storm.
ui.presentation.mars11: Sol 11: a communications antenna keeps the link with Earth.
ui.presentation.marsStorm: Solar storm on Mars: the crew goes into the shelter.
ui.presentation.marsWin: The Mars colony is self-sufficient. Mission accomplished!
ui.presentation.ending: Ending: the crew stays on Mars to keep the colony running.
ui.presentation.end: End of the presentation. Thank you! Press X to watch it again.

ui.presentation.loseStart: Defeat demo: what happens if the crew ignores life support? Press Z at any time to stop.
ui.presentation.lose1: Day 1: the crew only thinks about solar panels. Nobody plans water, air or food.
ui.presentation.lose2: Day 2: a battery and a mineral… but still no oxygen generator and no water.
ui.presentation.lose3: Day 3: more panels. Look at the warning over the astronaut: the reserves are falling.
ui.presentation.lose4: Day 4: the crew walks around the base without a plan.
ui.presentation.lose5: Day 5: only 2 days of oxygen left! The warning turns red, but nobody listens.
ui.presentation.lose6: Day 6: mission control insists. Still no oxygen generator and no water extractor.
ui.presentation.lose7: Day 7: the oxygen and the water have run out. The crew is in serious danger.
ui.presentation.loseStorm: A solar storm arrives, and the crew does not even go into the shelter.
ui.presentation.loseBoom: Life support failed. Without air, water and protection, the mission ends in disaster.
ui.presentation.loseLesson: Lesson: air and water come first, then power, food and protection. Press X to watch the mission done right.
ui.controls.z: Z — defeat demo (what happens if you ignore life support)
ui.presentation.speedHint: Mouse wheel up to speed up, down to slow down. Each show starts at normal speed.
ui.presentation.boarding: The crew climbs aboard the ship and lifts off from the Moon.
ui.presentation.flight: On the way to Mars: months of travel in deep space.
ui.presentation.arrival: Landing on Mars: a second ship arrives with two more crew members. "We came to help!" Now there are six.

ui.presentation.design1: Mission design: every mission starts on Earth. First, the objective: a self-sufficient Moon base.
ui.presentation.design2: The launch vehicle: a medium rocket balances cost and how much mass it can lift.
ui.presentation.design3: The payload: water and food for the first days, a radiation sensor for early storm warnings and a tool kit for repairs.
ui.presentation.design4: Within budget and under the mass limit. Launch!
ui.presentation.loseDesign1: Defeat demo: the mission planners cut corners from the very start.
ui.presentation.loseDesign2: The cheapest rocket and the slowest trajectory, to save money.
ui.presentation.loseDesign3: They pack materials and a battery… but no oxygen, water or food.
ui.presentation.loseDesign4: It fits the budget, but the plan ignores life support. Launch!
